evidence: src/app/access/access.controller.ts createAccess: `if (this.configurationService.get('ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION') && this.request.user.subscription.type === 'Basic') throw new HttpException(FORBIDDEN)`
src/app/access/access.controller.ts updateAccess: the same ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION / 'Basic' subscription check is repeated verbatim

src/app/access/access.controller.ts deleteAccess and updateAccess: both run `const originalAccess = await this.accessService.access({ id, userId: this.request.user.id }); if (!originalAccess) throw FORBIDDEN`
src/app/access/access.controller.ts getAllAccesses: `@UseGuards(AuthGuard('jwt'), HasPermissionGuard)` without @HasPermission, unlike the other handlers
src/app/access/access.module.ts: AccessModule only registers AccessController/AccessService and imports ConfigurationModule and PrismaModule, so it is cohesive
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files are cohesive: AccessModule wires AccessController and AccessService, and every controller handler deals with access grants. However, the controller copies business rules that should each live in one place. The subscription-tier gating rule (ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION && subscription.type === 'Basic' → 403) appears word for word in both createAccess and updateAccess. The ownership rule (accessService.access({ id, userId: request.user.id }) and 403 if missing) is copied in deleteAccess and updateAccess. Both rules are written inline in the controller instead of being kept in AccessService or a guard. That bypasses the module's own gating mechanism (HasPermission/HasPermissionGuard) and means the rules must be kept in sync by hand. getAllAccesses also uses HasPermissionGuard without any @HasPermission decorator, which is inconsistent with the other handlers. The module file itself is fine.

violations.message: The subscription-tier rule (ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION && subscription.type === 'Basic' → 403) is copied in createAccess and updateAccess instead of living in one place (a guard or AccessService).
The ownership rule (accessService.access({ id, userId }) and FORBIDDEN if missing) is copied in deleteAccess and updateAccess instead of being kept in one place in AccessService or a guard.
